subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: baseline + soft-fallback options for Cyphertia
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cyphertia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: baseline + soft-fallback options for Cyphertia

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Attached is a concise options set for a dedicated reservation that matches the usage profile you shared (spikey inference during ingest windows, sustained low-traffic inference otherwise). I tried to give three distinct pathways so your procurement and infra teams can choose trade-offs between cost predictability and burst flexibility.

High-level (numbers are A100-equivalent GPU units):
- Option A — Baseline Guarantee: 8 min GPUs (soft floor) + 24 active cluster (initial) ramping to 40 over 90 days. Best for predictable latency and simpler autoscale rules.
- Option B — Hybrid Floor + Burst: 4 min GPUs guaranteed, 32 active cluster with a 40-gpu burst lane (pay-as-you-go beyond baseline) and 200k warmup token credits to reduce cold-start overhead. Ramp: 4 -> 32 active across 60 days, burst available day 1.
- Option C — Aggressive Onramp with Holdback: 12 min GPUs, 48 active cluster but with a 25% holdback pool (warm standby for fast failover). Ramp triggers tied to throughput thresholds (50% utilization sustained for 7d).

Key behavioral notes:
- Warmup credits: prefix/KV cache priming reduces per-token cost during day-1 spikes. We put suggested credit allotments in the attached spreadsheet.
- Soft-fallbacks: if the primary model lane is constrained we can automatically route to a quantized variant (Q4_8) with slightly lower latency but substantial cost savings; this is configurable per-route.
- Activation triggers: recommend milestone-based activations (usage or monthly commit) rather than hard dates to reduce risk of paying for unused capacity.

Next asks from our side: procurement timeline, preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly reserve), and whether you want the holdback pool enabled in Option C.

I'll schedule a quick sync for Thursday; Marissa, Sean — please chime in if anything should be adjusted before I send a formal quote.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: capacity_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx)
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cyphertia.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <infra@cyphertia.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: baseline + soft-fallback options for Cyphertia

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear options. A couple of clarifying questions from infra and procurement:  
1) For Option B, how fast can burst capacity be provisioned and what are the committed vs. metered rates? We need to understand worst-case spend on a heavy ingest day.  
2) For the soft-fallback to quantized variants: what is the expected change in latency and token-level quality drop (we need a short SLA note for our reliability team)?  
3) Contract term: our procurement prefers a net-45 invoice on committed monthly payment. Is that doable?

Also, can you add a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestone owners and dates so our PMs can align? If possible, include a one-page operational runbook for the first 30 days — especially cache priming steps.

We can take the Thursday sync — 11am PT works.

Thanks,
Alicia Park
Head of Platform, Cyphertia
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cyphertia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: baseline + soft-fallback options for Cyphertia

Alicia — thanks, answers inline and added the requested MAP + runbook as a short attachment in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcdExample/view?usp=sharing 

1) Burst provisioning & rates: burst capacity is available within 2–10 minutes for pre-warmed lanes; cold provision can take ~20–45 minutes depending on region. Pricing: committed baseline priced at $/gpu-hour in the spreadsheet; burst beyond reserved capacity billed at our metered rate (we included a capped daily burn estimate for the 95th percentile traffic day in the sheet). We can add a hard daily cap for an added fee if procurement wants spend-safety gating.

2) Soft-fallback impact: quantized Q4_8 variant typically increases token latency by ~5–12% (median) and has a perceptible but small drop in certain open-ended generation tasks (we measured 90–95% semantic parity on your evaluation prompts). We can map route-level fallbacks and provide an immediate rollback if quality monitors (we integrate with your eval set) detect >3% regression. Note: we will include the fallback behavior in the SLA appendix.

3) Net-45 invoicing: yes, procurement terms with net-45 are acceptable for committed customers; I'll bubble that to finance and include it in the draft.

Quick MAP (high level):
- Week 0 (procurement & legal): finalize billing cadence (Alicia / Cyphertia PM), sign SOW (Redwood Legal) — target: +14 days
- Week 1 (infra onboarding): account-level keys, VPC peering, initial prefix cache mapping (Dev Ops + Redwood SRE) — target: +7 days after SOW
- Weeks 2–6 (ramp): staged activation (low -> baseline -> burst tests) with daily burn verification and load tests (Dev Ops / Redwood Solutions)
- Week 8 (stabilize): finalize autoscale rules and QA signoff

Attachments: capacity_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx (pricing by option), SLA_exceptions_draft.pdf (fallback/SLO language).

Marissa / Sean — please review the MAP and pricing sheet; highlight any gaps (especially around holdback semantics in Option C).

I'll send a formal quote after we confirm billing cadence and the holdback decision.

-Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cyphertia.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: baseline + soft-fallback options for Cyphertia

Alicia — quick note ahead of the 11am sync: based on the usage traces you shared, our recommendation is Option B (Hybrid Floor + Burst) with a protective daily cap and the 200k warmup credits enabled. That gives you the fastest path to handle ingest spikes while keeping committed spend lower. If procurement wants the simplest accounting, we can convert the burst lane into a small overage slab (e.g., 8 GPUs at a reduced metered rate) so you get fixed budgeting for typical spikes.

I'll bring a one-pager that maps cost scenarios at 25/50/90/99 percentile traffic to the meeting. See you Thursday.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: cost_scenarios_onepager.pdf)
